transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! I'm doing okay, thank you. I do have a few questions about my recovery. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can start doing light gardening activities, like watering or pruning, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting or bending for a month. If you're unsure, it's always best to check with your care team for personalized advice.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can start using your preservative-free eye drops, which are for dry eyes, four times daily to start. If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. You can also get more eye drops from your GP if you need to.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's normal to have some sensitivity to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's severe or you also have redness and pain, we may need to assess it further. If it's just mild and things seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside can help.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?
transcript.delivered: It's normal to have some sensitivity to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You might also want to consider wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. That should help.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness, especially in the first week after surgery. But it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thanks for answering my questions, Dora.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. I hope you have a smooth recovery. I'll just check in with you one more time: do you feel like all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I feel like all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!
